paper.title: Do You Think What I Think? A Qualitative Study for Maximising User Engagement through Latent Visual Properties
paper.abstract: Designing creative and reflective data visualisations offers the potential to move beyond static representations by incorporating latent visual properties (LVP) that stimulate insight, creativity, and decision-making. While traditional visualisations emphasize clarity and precision, they often overlook visual characteristics that are not directly visible in raw data but play an essential role in user engagement and sense-making. This study investigates how such LVP emerge and can be leveraged during the visualisation design process. We conducted a qualitative study combining a hands-on visualisation workshop and expert interviews to examine how participants interpret, reflect on, and redesign visualisations within a transdisciplinary context. The workshop involved nine participants working on a retail discount-optimization task, where they explored visualisation practices, identified LVP, and evaluated related design principles. Follow-up interviews with six domain experts validated the relevance and applicability of the resulting property-mapping strategies, including ignorance mapping (cognitive load awareness), creative unblocking (dynamic filtering and interactivity), and symbolic representation (emotive colour encoding and empathy mapping).
